title: Personal LLM experiment mini-sheet (Taylor)
content:
Mini experiment tracker - quick reference table and notes

Purpose: keep a compact, portable record of quick LLM inference experiments (prompt variants, hyperparams, quick quality/check metrics) that I can copy into PRs or Slack threads. Not meant to be canonical results - use eval harness for final.

Table columns: id | date | model | prompt_variant | temp | top_p | batch | seq_len | tokens_in | tokens_out | latency_ms_median | cost_est_usd | metric_note | status

Rows:
1 | 2026-01-12 | redwood-oasst-7b | baseline-short | 0.7 | 0.9 | 1 | 256 | 45 | 120 | 180 | 0.0021 | fluency ok, halluc small | WIP
2 | 2026-01-18 | redwood-oasst-7b-quant | baseline-short | 0.7 | 0.9 | 4 | 256 | 45 | 120 | 220 | 0.0009 | throughput better, quality ~equal | WIP
3 | 2026-02-05 | redwood-oasst-7b | prompt-v2-context | 0.3 | 0.8 | 1 | 512 | 140 | 210 | 340 | 0.0050 | reduced halluc, slightly longer latency | review
4 | 2026-02-20 | redwood-13b | prompt-v2-context | 0.3 | 0.8 | 1 | 512 | 140 | 210 | 520 | 0.0125 | best quality but cost high | draft

Quick notes / observations:
- Quantized 7B (row 2) gives ~2.5x throughput at ~same perceived quality on quick spot-checks. Good candidate for default for low-latency endpoints.
- Prompt-v2-context (rows 3-4) reduces factual errors for this FAQ-style prompts set; increases token usage due to longer context.
- Latency numbers are median p50 measured from local dev bench against dedicated-dev pool; not production SLOs. Use Redwood Console dashboards for production.

TODOs:
- [ ] Run eval harness for prompt-v2-context across 200 eval items (ticket ENG-2147).
- [ ] Add automated job to log tokens_in/out to S3 and compute cost per query (see GH PR linked).
- [ ] Try batch=8 for quantized 7B to see latency vs throughput tradeoff (esp. tail).

Scratchpad (random):
- Hypothesis: reducing temp to 0.2 + prompt-v2-context will cut hallucinations by ~15% but may harm creativity; run 100-sample A/B.
- Slack snippet for #eng-ml: "quick micro-bench: 7b-quant gives 2.5x throughput vs fp16, quality looks comparable on our FAQ set — can reduce cost for low-sensitivity endpoints".
- Links to artifacts: ENG-2147 (eval job), PR #86 (mini automation for cost calc), confluence page for eval-runbook.

Versioning / provenance notes:
- Keep this sheet for quick copy-paste; final numbers for any external doc should reference eval harness run ids and Redwood Console dashboards.
- If I merge a prompt change to prompts/main, update this sheet note with PR link and date.

Last quick log: 2026-02-28 - moved prompt-v2-context from "notes" to table row 3 after manual review of 50 samples; flagged for formal eval.
